 IMD Red Orange Alert: 14 States Face Rain, Cold Winds & Temperature Drop
 Odisha floods affect 3 districts, 62,000 people stranded: Cyclone Arnab triggers storms, rain in MP, UP & Rajasthan; orange alert in 14 states
 11 hours ago 
 Copy link 
 Cyclonic storm Arnab has weakened into a low-pressure area. Despite this, thunderstorms and rain continue across 14 states, including Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued red and orange alerts for these states for the next two days. Rain and cold winds have caused daytime temperatures to drop in several states.
 Flooding has affected three districts of Odisha — Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal. Around 300 villages in Ganjam have been cut off. Nearly 62,000 people are stranded in flood-hit areas of Ganjam and Gajapati districts. NDRF teams have airlifted 120 people so far.
 Delhi received rain late on Thursday night. According to the IMD, the maximum temperature on Thursday was recorded at 25.4°C, which was 6.4°C lower than the previous day. It was also the lowest maximum temperature recorded in October in the past four years.
 A high alert was issued in West Bengal's Alipurduar and Cooch Behar due to the possibility of flooding in the Sankosh River. Weather pictures from across the country... 
 Storm Arnab's impact has reached northern and north-western India. In Patna, people make their way through waterlogged roads amid the rain. In Delhi's Sarojini Nagar, water was sprayed from sprinklers to reduce dust pollution amid vehicular movement. Heavy snowfall occurred near Gangotri Dham in Uttarkashi. The snowfall has further intensified the cold in the area. The paddy crop in Raipur was destroyed by rain and strong winds caused by the cyclone. Motorcycles lie submerged in water after the flash flood caused by 'Cyclone Arnab' in Bhanjanagar. Due to the cyclone, the Howrah-Chennai railway track was submerged in water in Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh. A drone photograph of the flooded area of Berhampur in Ganjam, Odisha. Flooding after the rain has affected normal life here. Rescue workers brought a woman to safety amid the flash floods caused by Cyclone Arnab in Bhanjanagar. People wade through a waterlogged area amid flash flooding caused by Cyclone 'Arnab' in Berhampur, Odisha. Kedarnath in Rudraprayag, Uttarakhand, has been blanketed by heavy snowfall. Despite the biting cold, a large number of pilgrims have gathered here. Weather forecast for October 31 and November 1 
 October 31: A yellow alert has been issued for rainfall in Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema. Strong winds are also expected in Andhra Pradesh.
 November 1: A yellow alert has been issued for rainfall in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Karnataka, Rayalaseema and Andhra Pradesh.
